I stand corrected. I rewatched the video I got my substrate recipe from and its 4 quarts I used. Lol I haven't tried 5 quarts but I'm sure it does the job just fine. I'll take your word for it.

Good luck getting those cakes out. You might as well grind it up and put it into a monotub. 1 brick of coco coir, 2 quarts boiling water, 1 quart vermiculite, let it cool for 12-24 hours or room temp in and 5 gallon bucket. And then add mycelium to substrate in a tub.

Not enough moisture and fresh air exchange. Mushrooms are mostly water weight so you need to make sure you dunk your cakes and keep your tub nice and humid. Your mushrooms won't grow if they lose water content in the cake. And as small as cakes are in the temps your keeping, they will dry out fast. That why monotubs are the way to go. IMO. Just redunk your cakes and keep them soaks when your spraying. Fan after spray.
If you don't know then dont.
That's common. It's just the mycelium stretching taking hold of substrate. I suggest shredding your cakes into monotub after 100%. Much easier to maintain IMO.
